NoteTexAccessor::collapse_macros¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::collapse_macros() const

Remove Local Declarations Without Expanding Use Sites¶

collapse_macros() reduces declaration-heavy fragments to compact canonical source. For every cell it removes complete \newcommand, \renewcommand, \providecommand, and \def declarations; applies the built-in spelling normalizations from canonicalize_macros(); then collapses ASCII whitespace and trims both ends.

The operation intentionally does not substitute a removed definition at its use sites. If a cell declares \RR and later contains \RR, the use remains \RR. This makes collapse_macros() appropriate when declarations are metadata to discard but symbolic source should remain symbolic. Use macro_subs() when the body must replace every use before the declaration is removed.

Declaration parsing is brace-aware. Nested bodies such as \newcommand{\RR}{\mathbb{R}} and parameterized definitions such as \def\pair#1#2{{#1,#2}} are removed as complete units rather than leaving a suffix behind. Malformed or unterminated declarations are retained because there is no safe declaration boundary to erase.

Whitespace normalization is consequential: spaces, tabs, line feeds, carriage returns, form feeds, and vertical tabs become one ordinary space, including whitespace that may be meaningful to a downstream TeX formatter. The method is therefore a compact-source transform, not merely a declaration filter. It does not remove comments or external definitions.

The result owns fresh Text storage and preserves rank, shape, and cell order. Undefined propagates; empty and declaration-only cells become empty strings. Non-Text Notes reject. Parsing and whitespace normalization are linear in source size, aside from the bounded lookup of the twelve canonical built-ins.

Example 1: Nested newcommand Body And Surviving Use Site¶

const auto documents = pluss::make_note({
    "  \\newcommand{\\RR}{\\mathbb{R}}\n"
    "  \\dfrac{1}{2}   in   \\RR  ",
    R"(\def\pair#1#2{{#1,#2}}
        \tfrac{x}{y})"});
std::cout << documents.tex().collapse_macros() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["\\frac{1}{2} in \\RR", "\\frac{x}{y}"]

Both declarations disappear, fraction spellings become canonical, and the first cell’s \RR use remains unresolved by design.

Example 2: Native Integer Cells Reject¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().collapse_macros();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "collapse Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

collapse Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • canonicalize_macros: normalize built-ins without removing declarations.

  • macro_subs: substitute locally defined bodies before discarding declarations.

  • Note::collapse_whitespace: whitespace-only normalization on the root text surface.
